about: Known-good speed and memory (root CLAUDE.md, Metrics and baselines), checked on every pull request by .github/scripts/baseline.py (ci.yml, job baseline). Metric names are app.<operation>.<kind> (the kernel's own metrics moved with it to its private repo on 2026-10-27, values unchanged); the kind picks the margin. Update the values only when the owner confirms a change is intended: python3 .github/scripts/baseline.py --update. Values are from GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners. The same file holds the magic-moment journeys (journeys_about, journeys).
journeys_about: Magic-moment journeys (X8, packages/testing/src/magic.ts): the most clicks and the slowest of 5 walks in Chromium on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners, confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-16; re-measured that day as the slowest of 12 five-walk runs on 4 runners (0.19-1.23 s). Design: shape to STL went to 4 clicks on 2026-10-24 (owner's OK, presets moved into Insert ▾, U0d) and its time was re-measured on 2026-10-25 UTC as the slowest of 12 five-walk runs (0.44-1.16 s). apps/fission/e2e/journeys.mjs fails on any extra click (every run) and, nightly (JOURNEY_NIGHTLY=1), on a slowest walk more than twice the baseline or, on a branch, more than 30% slower than main's build walked in turns on the same runner; more than 15% over either is flagged as a warning (runners differ by more than that: 1.35-1.65 s against 1.16 s on 2026-10-26/27).

instructions.why: callgrind's count of instructions executed: the same on every run to about 0.05%, so any real slowdown shows; 15% is the project's performance margin

peak_bytes.why: most extra heap at once, from a counting allocator: exact, so 15% catches real growth

retained_bytes.why: JavaScript heap a result keeps after a full GC; the floor absorbs the engine's own few kilobytes of noise

wasm_bytes.why: the kernel's WebAssembly memory high-water mark, in 64 KiB pages; one page of slack

relative_time.why: time divided by a fixed JavaScript workload's in the same process; still varies by about 15% between runs and machines, so past 15% it only warns, and only twice as slow fails

kernel_calls.why: every kernel call one edit makes (step 24d3c, packages/testing/baseline/rebuild.ts): exact, so 15%, the project's margin, lets a few calls more pass and fails a waste on every feature (20 more on the 20-feature part)

body_builds.why: bodies the kernel builds for one edit: exact; a working cache builds only the edited feature's body, so any more means unchanged features are being rebuilt

miss_percent.why: held references the naming sessions resolved otherwise than the model says (lost, moved, or found on two faces), as a percent of those checked, so 0 is a 100% naming success rate (step 25b4, packages/testing/baseline/naming.ts); any miss is a naming bug, so any rise from 0 fails (owner, 2026-10-21)

wrong_percent.why: steps of the seeded timeline sessions whose rebuild the model disagrees with, as a percent of the steps run (step 30d, Tier 3's simulated users, packages/testing/baseline/naming.ts), so 0 is 100% of rebuilds right; a session stops at its first wrong rebuild, so any rise from 0 is a bug and fails

invalid_percent.why: the kernel's body_build answers in the same sessions that failed validate or crashed, as a percent of those answered (step 30d), so 0 is 100% of bodies passing validate; any is a kernel bug, so any rise from 0 fails

failed_percent.why: golden models whose rebuild differs from their hand-worked answers, as a percent of those that build today (step 28b, packages/testing/baseline/golden.ts), so 0 is a 100% golden success rate; any wrong answer is a bug, so any rise from 0 fails
